A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel indoor point cloud segmentation framework called PGCNet, which treats patches of the point cloud as input graph nodes, and dynamically aggregates node features by DGU module.
we have developed a novel indoor point cloud segmentation network that is able to achieve competitive segmentation accuracy while being much faster than the state of the art.

we proposed a novel framework to segment indoor scenes into room layout and indoor object categories by using patch graph convolution network, and the proposed framework achieves comparable performance to state of the arts with a significant speed up in training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patch based graph convolution network is an efficient and powerful framework for segmenting indoor scenes.
patch based representation is a more efficient way to represent point cloud data, and dynamic graph convolution is an effective way to encode hierarchical patch features.
surface patches are a more efficient representation than individual sampling points, which can be further extended to various other tasks such as point cloud classification.
